source: FORM form_cues (live app copy, Nov 17 2026). Only cues with a finished drawing are published.
practice: On easy runs, think about it for 30 seconds, three times. Then run normally and notice the difference. In hard workouts, use it on the last rep.

cues.name: Long neck
cues.do: Keep your chin level. Look at the ground a little way ahead.
cues.think: Pretend a string is gently pulling the top of your head up to the sky. Your chin stays level, never up.
cues.why: A high chin bends your back and tightens your shoulders. A long neck keeps you tall and makes breathing easy.
cues.alt: A runner from the side, tall, with a level chin and eyes a little way ahead.
cues.try: Stand with your back on a wall. Touch the wall with the back of your head without lifting your chin. Run at that height.
cues.feel: Your neck feels long and your shoulders drop.

cues.name: Quiet shoulders
cues.do: Keep your shoulders low and still. Only your arms swing.
cues.think: Pretend there is a full cup of water on each shoulder. Don't spill a drop.
cues.why: Bouncy shoulders push you up instead of forward, and they make your neck tight.
cues.alt: A runner from the front with level, relaxed shoulders while the arms swing.
cues.try: Shrug your shoulders up to your ears, then let them fall. Where they land is where they stay.
cues.feel: Your neck stays loose, even late in the run.

cues.name: Four lights
cues.do: Keep your shoulders right on top of your hips.
cues.think: Pretend you have headlights on your shoulders and tail lights on your hips. Keep all four lights pointing straight ahead, never crossing.
cues.why: When your shoulders twist side to side, you waste energy. Facing forward sends all of it forward.
cues.alt: A runner from the front, with small lights marking both shoulders and both hips, all square and facing forward.
cues.try: Watch yourself run toward a shop window, or film ten seconds from the front. Shoulders and hips face the same way the whole time.
cues.feel: Your chest faces forward and your arms swing past your sides, not across your body.

cues.name: Elbows back
cues.do: Push your elbows back. Let them swing forward on their own.
cues.think: Pretend someone is standing right behind you. Bump them gently with each elbow.
cues.why: Your legs copy your arms. Arms that push back push you forward.
cues.alt: A runner from the side driving one elbow back behind the body.
cues.try: Stand still and swing your arms. Push back firmly and let the forward swing be easy. Notice your legs want to go.
cues.feel: The work happens behind you, and your hands stay relaxed.

cues.name: Low hands
cues.do: Keep your hands low, close to your hips.
cues.think: Reach for your shorts pockets every time your arm swings back.
cues.why: High hands make your shoulders tight. Low, loose hands let your arms help your legs.
cues.alt: A runner with loose hands passing low, close to the hips.
cues.try: Bend your elbows to about a right angle and swing so your thumbs brush the side of your shorts.
cues.feel: Your shoulders sink and your arms feel lighter.

cues.name: Soft hands
cues.do: Keep your hands loose, never in a fist.
cues.think: Pretend you are holding a potato chip in each hand. Don't break it.
cues.why: Tight fists make tight arms and shoulders. Soft hands let the whole upper body relax.
cues.alt: A runner from the front with loose, relaxed hands.
cues.try: Squeeze a tight fist for five seconds, then open it halfway. Run with the halfway hand.
cues.feel: Your forearms and shoulders stay loose.

cues.name: Hips forward
cues.do: Run tall with your hips forward, right under your shoulders.
cues.think: Pretend a rope is tied to your belt buckle, gently pulling you forward. Your hips go first and your feet follow.
cues.why: When your hips sit back, your legs do all the work. Hips forward lets your glutes push you along.
cues.alt: A runner from the side, tall, with a thin orange rope pulling forward from the belt buckle.
cues.try: Stand tall and lean your whole body forward from the ankles until you have to take a step. That first step is the feeling.
cues.feel: Your glutes push you along and each step feels easier.

cues.name: Tall spring
cues.do: Run tall and let each foot bounce off the ground fast.
cues.think: The floor is lava. Each foot taps it and snaps straight back up, like a piston.
cues.why: The longer your foot sits on the ground, the more energy it soaks up. A quick tap lets the spring in your legs push you forward.
cues.alt: A tall runner from the side with a light coil drawn around the standing leg.
cues.try: Run in place on lava for 10 seconds: quick taps, soft knees, body tall. Then run 20 steps the same way.
cues.feel: Light and bouncy. You hear a quick tap, not a slap.

cues.name: Land under you
cues.do: Let each foot land right under your hips, not out in front.
cues.think: Pretend there is a coin on the ground right under your hips. Step on the coin.
cues.why: A foot that lands far in front puts on the brakes. Landing under you keeps you rolling forward.
cues.alt: A runner from the side with the front foot landing under the hips, on a small coin.
cues.try: Run on the spot for ten seconds. Your feet land right under you. Now drift forward and keep landing there.
cues.feel: Your steps get a little shorter, quicker and quieter.

cues.name: Quick feet
cues.do: Take light, quick steps. Your feet leave the ground fast.
cues.think: Pretend the ground is hot. Touch it and get your foot off fast.
cues.why: Quick, light steps spend less time braking and put less pounding on your legs.
cues.alt: A runner from the side, one foot barely touching the ground with small heat lines under it.
cues.try: Count your right foot for 30 seconds. Then add two or three more steps at the same speed.
cues.feel: Lighter, quieter steps, as if you are barely touching the ground.

cues.name: Straight feet
cues.do: Point your toes straight ahead when each foot lands.
cues.think: Pretend you are running on two train tracks, one for each foot. Keep your toes on the tracks.
cues.why: A foot that turns out pushes you sideways. Straight feet push you forward and keep your knees happy.
cues.alt: A runner from the front with both feet landing pointed straight ahead.
cues.try: Run along a painted line. Each foot lands on its own side of it, toes pointing straight down the line.
cues.feel: Your knees travel straight ahead, over your toes.
